title: Hopkins Man Charged With Attempted Murder in Attack on Uber Driver Mohamed Yusuf
excerpt: Samit Apurva Patel, 25, is held on $1 million bail after prosecutors say he strangled Somali American driver Mohamed Yusuf with a seatbelt and ran him over with his own car. Yusuf, 51, is in critical condition, and prosecutors say bias could not be proved beyond a reasonable doubt.
body:
• Samit Apurva Patel, 25, of Hopkins, Minnesota, was charged on Tuesday, November 17, with attempted second-degree murder and first-degree carjacking, and is being held on $1 million bail, according to prosecutors and court documents.
  • Mohamed Yusuf, 51, a Somali American Uber driver, is in critical condition with broken ribs, a broken leg, spinal injuries, collapsed lungs and significant internal bleeding; the criminal complaint says his prognosis is poor, and his family says he is in a coma.
  • Prosecutors said the evidence could not prove beyond a reasonable doubt that bias motivated the attack. Yusuf's family and the Minnesota chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations describe the attack as hate-driven and have called for a federal hate-crime review.
  • To help: Yusuf's family is raising money for his medical care through a GoFundMe campaign that had raised more than $330,000 as of Monday, November 16, according to FOX 9.

A 25-year-old Uber passenger has been charged with attempted murder in a weekend attack near Minneapolis that left a Somali American driver strangled with a seatbelt, run over by his own car and found in a roadside ditch, authorities said. Samit Apurva Patel of Hopkins was charged on Tuesday, November 17, with one count of attempted second-degree murder and one count of first-degree carjacking for the November 14 attack on Mohamed Yusuf, 51, the Hennepin County Attorney's Office said. Indian news outlets, including The Times of India, identified Patel as Indian-origin.

Yusuf has broken ribs, a broken leg, spinal injuries, collapsed lungs and significant internal bleeding, and several of his organs had to be removed, according to the criminal complaint. His prognosis is poor, the complaint says. His family said in a GoFundMe appeal that he remains in a coma and is fighting for his life, writing that "he was simply trying to earn an honest living and return home safely to his loved ones."

What the complaint says happened

Yusuf was on the phone with his brother, who is also an Uber driver, when he picked up the passenger just before 1 a.m. on Saturday, November 14, according to court documents. His brother told investigators he heard the passenger ask Yusuf his name and, after Yusuf identified himself as Mohamed, say he did not like that name. The brother later heard Yusuf screaming in Somali that he was being choked with a belt and run over by the car, according to the filing.

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty said the motive remains unknown. Patel's parents called 911 for a wellness check after he arrived home appearing intoxicated and "exhibiting signs of emotional distress and belligerent behavior," according to the court filing. When officers arrived, they found Yusuf's car in the driveway, its exterior and driver's seatbelt damaged, with the phone call to Yusuf's brother still active through the car's system. Officers said Patel told them he had been drinking and admitted he took an Uber home, but claimed not to know where his driver was, the filing says.

Officers found Yusuf in a patch of burs in a ditch off the side of the road near Hopkins Crossroad and Minnetonka Boulevard, using location data from his smartwatch and a drone with thermal imaging, according to court documents.

"It was an incredibly brutal attack."

— Mary Moriarty, Hennepin County Attorney

Charges filed, bias enhancement declined

Patel made his first court appearance on Tuesday and is being held on $1 million bail, according to the Associated Press report carried by CNN. Online court records do not list an attorney for Patel; an attorney representing him at the appearance declined to comment.

Moriarty said prosecutors reviewed the evidence and determined there was "insufficient evidence to prove to a jury beyond reasonable doubt that a specific bias was the motivation for Mr. Patel's actions," while adding that this "does not diminish the pain that the family and the Somali community are feeling right now." Minnesota does not have a standalone hate-crime statute but allows enhanced sentencing for crimes motivated by bias. Moriarty said prosecutors have other legal tools available to seek a sentence reflecting the severity of the alleged offense if Patel is convicted.

Fear and support in the Somali community

The attack, in the Minneapolis suburb of Hopkins, has increased fear among Somali Americans, said Jaylani Hussein, executive director of the Minnesota chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR-MN), which has called for a federal hate-crime investigation. "We feel as a community we're under threat, constantly," Hussein said. Supporters demonstrated outside Hennepin County Medical Center on Monday, where Yusuf is being treated.

Uber said in a statement that it was horrified by the attack, has been in touch with the driver's family and has banned the rider from the platform.

How to help Yusuf's family

Yusuf's family is raising money through a GoFundMe campaign to help cover medical expenses, household bills, rehabilitation and potential long-term care. The campaign had raised more than $330,000 as of Monday, November 16, FOX 9 reported.

What happens next

Patel remains in custody on $1 million bail. The charges are allegations, and the case will proceed in Hennepin County District Court.
